title: How Can Generative AI Be Used in Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience?
summary: Learn how generative AI is being used in cybersecurity to help accelerate threat detection, improve ransomware response, support cyber recovery, and strengthen organizational resilience.
body_markdown:
## Why Is Cyber Resilience Becoming More Important Than Prevention Alone?


The rise of AI is changing the economics of cyberattacks. Attackers can automate reconnaissance, scale phishing campaigns, generate convincing social engineering content, and accelerate malicious operations with unprecedented efficiency. Defenders are using AI as well, but the reality is that prevention alone can no longer guarantee security. The attack surface is expanding faster than most organizations can protect it, particularly as cloud services, SaaS applications, and AI-forward systems become increasingly interconnected.


Organizations must assume that some attacks will succeed.


This is where cyber resilience becomes essential. Resilience focuses on helping organizations detect incidents quickly, contain damage, maintain critical operations, and recover trusted data when disruptions occur. Rather than measuring success solely by how many attacks are blocked, resilient organizations evaluate how effectively they can continue operating when defenses are bypassed.


According to McKinsey, 78% of organizations now regularly use generative AI, yet only 17% report that AI contributes a meaningful share of business value or profit impact, highlighting the gap between adoption and sustainable outcomes. The report argues that security, governance, and resilience are critical foundations for turning AI investments into long-term business value.


Generative AI strengthens a resilience-focused strategy by helping organizations move from reactive response to proactive preparedness. AI can identify vulnerabilities, highlight operational risks, assist with security planning, detect anomalies, and improve recovery readiness before an incident occurs. It also can help security and IT teams model potential attack scenarios, evaluate recovery plans, and identify weaknesses in critical business processes.


Preventing every attack may be an unattainable goal, but the ability to adapt, recover, and continue operating will help position organizations against increasingly sophisticated threats. In an era where disruption is increasingly inevitable, resilience may become the most important cybersecurity capability of all.
